1 · take next event
sequence n
'now' := the event's
harness time

div.style: color: rgb(11, 27, 63) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 420px; text-align: center;

span.p:
2 · decide
reads state · no waiting · no I/O
classify turn · last writer wins
desired keys · result admission
operation lock · commit barrier

div.style: color: rgb(11, 27, 63) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 420px; text-align: center;

span.p:
3 · apply
the ONLY place
state changes
revision n → n+1

span.p:
4 · emit actions in order
advisory cancel before
its replacement call

span.p: INBOX · first-in first-out · the sequence number it assigns is the only total order

div.style: color: rgb(61, 42, 16) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 420px; text-align: center; width: 420px;

span.p:
WHY THERE ARE NO STATE RACES
• exactly one writer: apply
• workers never hold mutable state
• every result re-enters as an event and is checked at admission before it is used
• a step takes milliseconds, so an interruption never waits behind slow work

div.style: color: rgb(5, 46, 22) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 420px; text-align: center; width: 420px;

span.p:
LEAVES THE STEP ASYNCHRONOUSLY → back to the concurrent side above
tool calls · advisory cancels → harness · effect requests → reasoner, perception · timers armed · journal records
